newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen flat or down.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen flat or down.

text.p: Polish shares on Wednesday fell in low turnover for the third day running and analysts said the market should continue its flat-to-down trend into next month during the public offering of copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz.

"You can't expect big falls because plenty of stocks have become pretty cheap...so there should be a flat trend or a slight fall," said Tomasz Cwintal, an analyst at Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) brokerage.
KGHM's 1.3-1.7-billion-zloty IPO starts on June 30, the day large Bank Handlowy starts trade on the main market. KGHM starts bourse trade on July 10.
Analysts said smaller investors might seek to take quick profits next week at Handlowy's debut to buy KGHM.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.6 percent to 15,606.0 points and turnover fell 5.2 percent to 102 million zlotys ($31.5 million) on both markets. Gainers and losers were even at 42 stocks each and 23 stocks were flat.

Analysts said a central bank deputy head's Tuesday statement that Poland faced a gaping current account deficit and a Czech-style financial crisis in 1998 if it failed to balance next year's budget represented a longer-term threat.
On Wednesday the finance minister said current fiscal and monetary policy should keep the deficit at safe levels.
Analysts said low turnover exaggeraged falls by Wednesday loss leaders meat firm Farm Food, aluminium plant Kety and engineering firm Remak, down 9.1, 5.7 and 4.5 percent respectively.
But they said Farm Food was hurt by this year's weaker earnings and Remak by Wednesday's news it needed to cut staff amid Poland's construction boom.
